source.note: COUNT-SCALED MANA FRONTIER witness (ADR-0003 accretion). Oracle (VERIFIED against oracle-cards.json): 'Legendary Land — {T}: Add {G} for each creature you control.' Ground ports (dumps/card-ports.json): line0 emit:mana:green (stem=mana, tier=Amber, spans [4,43]) + line0 consume tap:self. The mana emit IS AST-derivable at stem+color level (emit:mana:green), so this projects a USABLE mana port — but with NO qty projected at all: the 'for each creature you control' count sits inside span [4,43] yet is NOT extracted as a quantity. Contrast devoted-druid.json ('{T}: Add {G}' -> {color:green, qty:1}): Gaea's Cradle is byte-identical to that witnessed green-mana emit EXCEPT for the quantity, which is the whole point. TWO stacked gaps: (1) PARSE — the count clause is swallowed; the parser derives a flat mana emit with no qty. (2) SCAFFOLD — the qty axis (bindable: X | that-many | up-to-N; values 1..4 / X / that-many / up-to-5) has NO value that expresses 'an amount equal to a board count'. A count-scaled amount is none of the licensed bindings: it is not X (a chosen cast-value), not that-many (bound to a preceding count in the SAME effect), and not up-to-N (a bounded firability choice); it is qty = |board subset matching a filter|, a new symbolic binding. NO qty value is invented in this gold (per rule discipline) — the qty attr is DELIBERATELY OMITTED and the needed axis value is surfaced as the scaffold question in the assertions. Chosen over Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx / Nyx Lotus because THEIR count-scaled 'devotion' line projects emit:unstructured (stem=None, fully parse-gated) — Gaea's Cradle is the smallest card whose count-scaled mana emit still projects a usable (flat-qty) mana port. This is the smallest honest single-card witness of the count-scaling gap; judge PENDING and no rollup regenerated (frontier map, no flow run).

Gaea's Cradle.note: the '{T}' activation cost (dump: consume tap:self). Same shape as devoted-druid.DD_TAP / kiki K2.

'Add {G} for each creature you control' (live label emit:mana:green, stem=mana). color=green is AST-derivable (dumps/card-ports.json line0). qty is DELIBERATELY OMITTED, NOT set to 1: the true quantity is count-scaled (= creatures you control) which is both (a) not parsed (no qty span extracted — flat mana emit) and (b) not expressible by any licensed qty binding (X | that-many | up-to-N). Omitting is honest to the parser's flat derivation and avoids inventing a qty value; qty:1 would falsely under-approximate to a single pip. The MISSING count-scaled qty is the documented gap — see the scaffold_question assertion.

assertions.because: emit:mana:green is AST-derivable (dumps/card-ports.json line0, stem=mana, color=green) — a usable mana port at stem+color level

PARSE gap: the 'for each creature you control' count is swallowed into span [4,43] but no qty is projected — the parser derives a flat mana emit with no quantity, indistinguishable at the qty axis from a single {G} (devoted-druid). Extracting the count clause into a qty span is the parser target.

SCAFFOLD gap surfaced (NOT resolved, NO value invented): the count-scaled amount (qty = |creatures you control|) is not any licensed qty binding (X | that-many | up-to-N). It needs a NEW symbolic qty value — a board-count binding, e.g. qty = { bind: 'per-object', filter: <object-query> } — so the qty axis can express 'an amount equal to a board count' (devotion to a color and 'for each Swamp/creature you control' are the same shape). This is a taxonomy decision for the scaffold owner, not authorable unilaterally.
